solutions.check: 30 entries, 60 crossings, 0 conflicts; answers matched to the grid by number, direction and length

clue.text: Be taken in by out-and-out rogue

definitions.note: used adjectivally, as in a rogue result

indicators.note: something taken in by another is held inside it, so the first piece goes within the second

parts.note: out-and-out means utter or downright, as does arrant

explanation.surface: Someone is fooled by a thorough scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be taken in' looks like being duped, but it is a placement instruction. 'rogue' looks like a noun but works as an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a rogue reading or element is one that deviates from the norm.

clue.text: Poisonous gas is near spill

indicators.note: to spill is to scatter, so these letters are tumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A toxic gas is close to leaking out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spill' looks like the gas escaping but rearranges IS NEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemistry: it is a highly toxic arsenic hydride gas.

clue.text: Partner that was thoughtful not going for a song

parts.note: a former partner is an ex
pensive means thoughtful

explanation.surface: A former partner who was reflective did not feel like singing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a song' is British idiom for very cheaply.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: something sold for a song is cheap, so not going cheaply means costly.

clue.text: Run over batting order

indicators.note: one piece placed over another covers it, enclosing it

parts.note: a route, such as a delivery round, is a run
in cricket the side batting is in

explanation.surface: A cricket side's batting order is altered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'batting order' looks like a single cricket phrase; 'batting' gives IN and 'order' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a routine is a fixed sequence or order of doing things.

clue.text: Ruler in Africa, say, stopping North American

indicators.note: a piece stopping another plugs a gap in it, so sits inside

parts.note: US means American
e.g. is the abbreviation meaning for example, signalled by say

explanation.surface: An African ruler, for example, blocks a North American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like a link word, as in 'for instance', but it supplies the abbreviation for 'for example'.
explanation.definitionFit: Historical title: the negus was the emperor of Ethiopia.

clue.text: Mistake ringleader for man in charge

parts.note: a gaffe is a social blunder or mistake
the leader, or first letter, of the word ring is R

explanation.surface: Someone confuses the leader of a gang with the person officially in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringleader' looks like a gang boss but supplies only the opening letter of 'ring'.
explanation.definitionFit: British informal: a gaffer is a boss or foreman in charge of workers.

clue.text: Island with empty grave for marshal

parts.note: Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde, Scotland

indicators.note: an emptied word loses its inside, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: An island with an open grave, prepared for a military marshal.
explanation.walkthrough: Arran is a Scottish island. 'marshal' looks like a military rank but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to marshal things is to set them out in order.

clue.text: Light, it's said, may be bent

indicators.note: it is said marks a word spoken aloud whose sound matches a different spelling

parts.note: a flare is a bright signal light

explanation.surface: A light, so people claim, might be bent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bent' looks like crooked but means a natural aptitude.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a bent for something is a natural talent or knack.

clue.text: Local trendies all over the shop

indicators.note: a British phrase for in disarray, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Fashionable people from the area are everywhere in the store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over the shop' means in a mess, rearranging TRENDIES. 'Local' looks like a pub but is a noun for an inhabitant.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a local is someone who lives in the area, an inhabitant.

clue.text: Not prepared for crops before light's provided

parts.note: until means up to the time of, before
an LED, light-emitting diode, is a light

explanation.surface: Land is not ready for farming until lighting is provided.
explanation.walkthrough: LED stands for light-emitting diode.
explanation.definitionFit: Farming: unploughed ground has not been readied for sowing.

clue.text: Spain guarantees resort for old folk

indicators.note: to re-sort is to sort again, so the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Spain promises a holiday resort for elderly people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday destination but is read as re-sort, rearranging SPAIN GUARANTEES.
explanation.definitionFit: People in their seventies are elderly, so they can loosely be called old folk.

clue.text: Name little orphan's carers

parts.note: Little Orphan Annie, the American comic-strip girl, so her name with possessive S

explanation.surface: Identify the people who looked after a small orphan.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Orphan Annie is a long-running American comic strip and musical character.
explanation.definitionFit: Nannies are paid childminders, people who look after children.

clue.text: Prince Edward's cloak for knight sent to Coventry?

indicators.note: a cloak wraps round its wearer, so the prince-plus-Edward letters go around the knight

parts.note: Prince Igor, the Russian prince of Borodin's opera
N is the chess notation for a knight
Ed is the short form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: A royal's cloak is handed to a knight who is being shunned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prince Edward' reads as one royal, but splits into Borodin's operatic prince and a short name. To 'send someone to Coventry' is a British idiom for refusing to speak to them.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: someone sent to Coventry is ostracised, deliberately left unspoken to and disregarded.

clue.text: No way to be happy in Hades?

definitions.meaning: to enjoy the underworld, read literally as being fond of the infernal place

explanation.surface: A refusal to be content in the underworld.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the phrase literally: to like the underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: Colloquial idiom: the phrase is an emphatic denial meaning certainly not; literally it is enjoying the inferno.

clue.text: Turning out European translation

parts.note: a version is a translation

explanation.surface: A European rendering of a text proves successful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning out' looks like resulting, but means turning inside out.
explanation.definitionFit: Medical term: the word means turning an organ or part outward, inside out.

clue.text: Don't patronise restaurant Escoffier's opening a can

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, so Escoffier gives his initial

parts.note: a can is a tin

explanation.surface: Even the great chef Escoffier opens a can rather than eat out.
explanation.walkthrough: Auguste Escoffier was a celebrated French chef, which colours the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to have dinner at home is the opposite of taking custom to a restaurant.

clue.text: Bird getting up to scratch round a tree

parts.note: a turkey is a bird

indicators.note: one piece going round another surrounds it

parts.note: OK means satisfactory, up to scratch

explanation.surface: A bird gets up to scratch around a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' is only a link; 'up to scratch' gives OK, which goes round A.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a Turkey oak is a deciduous oak species from southern Europe.

clue.text: Queue endlessly to get preservative

indicators.note: without its end, so the final letter of the phrase is dropped

parts.note: to queue is to form a line

explanation.surface: People line up endlessly to get a preservative.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemistry: a formaldehyde solution used to preserve biological specimens.

clue.text: Jockey having an advantage over another?

definitions.meaning: a rider is a single person mounted on a horse
being a point ahead of a rival

explanation.surface: A rider with an edge over a rival in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is literal: a jockey is one person up on horseback.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider is literally a single person mounted; the phrase also means holding a slight lead over a rival.

clue.text: One after another petition? Sound pleased about it

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the purr goes round the other piece

parts.note: a cat sounds pleased when it purrs
to sue is to petition or appeal

explanation.surface: Someone files one petition after another and is pleased with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One after another' looks like a sequence but means a chaser.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone chasing another person is after them.

clue.text: Complain after object is found with duck — a plum stone; for example

indicators.note: after places the complaining word at the end, following the other pieces

parts.note: an end is an aim or object
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O
to carp is to complain

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles after finding a duck paired with a plum stone.
explanation.walkthrough: The ';' is a print slip for a comma. A 'duck' is a cricket score of zero, hence O.
explanation.definitionFit: Botany: the hard inner layer around a fruit's seed, such as a plum stone, has this name.

clue.text: Go on about Nimrod?

parts.note: c, circa, means about
Nimrod is the mighty hunter of Genesis

explanation.surface: Talk endlessly about the biblical Nimrod.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reads as concerning but gives C (circa). Nimrod is the biblical 'mighty hunter'.
explanation.definitionFit: British informal: to chunter is to grumble or go on at length.

clue.text: Time for instruction in recipe

definitions.meaning: a period of the year, like summer
a cook is told to add salt and pepper

explanation.surface: It is time to follow the recipe's instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a period of the year and a cookery command to add flavouring.

clue.text: God ignoring outsiders in Christmas broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the remaining letters are rearranged
leaving out the outermost letters of the word Christmas, keeping its inner part

explanation.surface: A deity is left out of a Christmas radio broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' suggests radio, but rearranges HRISTMA, what is left once C and S go.
explanation.definitionFit: Mithras was a Persian deity whose cult was popular among Roman soldiers.

clue.text: Heavy footsteps heard in cargo boat

definitions.meaning: the sound of heavy, plodding steps
a merchant ship without a fixed route

explanation.surface: Heavy footsteps can be heard in a cargo ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a heavy tread and also a freighter that picks up cargo wherever it can.

clue.text: Rennet's first to be accepted by man before making cheese

indicators.note: one thing accepted by another is taken inside it

parts.note: a guy is a man

indicators.note: the first of Rennet is its opening letter

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A cheesemaker's rennet must first be approved by a man.
explanation.walkthrough: Rennet is used in cheesemaking, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Gruyère is a hard Swiss cheese.

clue.text: Dope — extremely rare type

parts.note: gen and dope are both slang for information

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Drugs of an extremely rare kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' suggests drugs but means information, GEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a genre is a kind or category, especially of art.

clue.text: Pacific group has disciplined a felonious agent

indicators.note: disciplined means put in order, so the letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A group of Pacific islands punished a criminal operative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pacific' reads as the ocean but means peaceable here.
explanation.definitionFit: Pacific means peace-making; the interwar body existed to preserve world peace.

clue.text: Linen not covering picture frame

indicators.note: one piece covering another is wrapped around it

parts.note: nary means not one, as in nary a word

indicators.note: the frame of a word is its outside letters

explanation.surface: Some linen is left draped off a picture frame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frame' takes P and E, the outside of 'picture', which NARY then encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: Napery is household linen, especially table linen such as napkins and cloths.

clue.text: Hide dukes and earls for starters then royal family?

indicators.note: starters are the first letters of dukes and earls

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher; with the possessive S it is the royal's
kin are relatives or family

explanation.surface: Dukes and earls go into hiding first, then the royal family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' reads as a verb but is the noun, an animal's skin. ER is the Queen's cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a hide is an animal's skin, and this one comes from a stag or doe.
